title: Floor Staircase
statement: How many of the integers $1, 2, \dots, 1000$ can be written as $\lfloor 2x\rfloor + \lfloor 4x\rfloor + \lfloor 6x\rfloor + \lfloor 8x\rfloor$ for some real number $x$?
solution: $f(x+\tfrac12) = f(x) + 10$. On $[0,\tfrac12)$, with breakpoints at $\tfrac18, \tfrac16, \tfrac14, \tfrac13, \tfrac38$, $f$ takes the values $0,1,2,4,5,6$. So $f$ hits exactly $6$ of every $10$ consecutive integers, and $600$ of $1, \dots, 1000$.
